# Page outlet: `jl-page-outlet`

Where the pages show: the next one loads out of sight, under a line, and shows once it has its data.

- Class `JlPageOutlet`, a organism: `import { JlPageOutlet } from '@syware/jlib';`
- On the site: https://bioleyl.github.io/jlib/components/page-outlet

A page outlet is where an app's pages show, one at a time. A new page loads out of sight while the
current one stays on screen, usable, under a line that says the next one is on its way (a jl-loading-bar). Once every
load state of the new page has its data, it takes the current one's place in one go: no half-drawn page, no skeleton
flashing between two pages. A page that takes longer than max-wait shows as it is, its load states with their
skeletons. The first page shows at once, as there is nothing to keep.

With a Jadis router, it shows the router's pages: router.mountOn(outlet, { show: (page) => outlet.show(page) }). It
goes where the pages go, in a jl-app-shell's main area for instance, flush with its top: the line runs along the top
edge of the outlet, so the room around a page belongs to the page, not to the area that holds the outlet. Under a
sticky bar, --line-top (the bar's height) keeps the line in sight once the page scrolls.

## Use

```ts
import { JlPageOutlet } from '@syware/jlib';
```

```tsx
<JlPageOutlet maxWait={3000}>
  <section style="padding: 16px">The page shown</section>
</JlPageOutlet>
```

```html
<jl-page-outlet max-wait="3000">
  <section style="padding: 16px">The page shown</section>
</jl-page-outlet>
```

## Properties

Inputs: a JSX prop sets one, code calls `.set(value)` and `.get()`, HTML writes the attribute (lists and objects as JSON).

- `maxWait` (attribute `max-wait`): `number`, default `3000`. The longest the current page stays while the next one loads, in milliseconds.

## Events

In JSX, the `on…` prop, its handler given the detail; in code, `events.register(name, (detail) => …)`. They do not bubble.

- `show` (`onShow` in JSX), detail `HTMLElement`: A page took its place, at the top of the outlet.

## Slots

- The default slot: The page shown. show() puts the pages there itself.
- `next`: The page loading, out of sight, until it takes its place.

## Methods

- `show(page: HTMLElement): void`: Shows a page: at once when none shows yet, else once its load states have their data (or after max-wait), the current page staying until then. A page still loading when another comes is dropped.

## Styling

- `--line-top` (custom property): How far from the top of the window the line stays once the page scrolls: the height of a sticky bar above the outlet. 0 by default.
- `line` (part, `::part(line)`): The jl-loading-bar over the page: its --color and --height.

## Examples

HTML as the site renders it, with its layout classes (`row`, `stack`, `narrow`, `muted`), which are not jlib's: a view writes the same components by class in JSX. A script's `root` is the example's element.

### From page to page

Orders takes 1.5 seconds, Customers 0.4: the page shown stays until the next has its rows. Press one, then the other at once: only the last one shows.

```html
<div class="stack">
  <div class="row">
    <jl-button class="to-orders" label="Orders"></jl-button>
    <jl-button class="to-customers" label="Customers"></jl-button>
  </div>
  <jl-page-outlet style="min-height: 180px; border: 1px solid var(--jl-line)"></jl-page-outlet>
</div>
```

```js
const outlet = root.querySelector('jl-page-outlet');
outlet.show(customersPage()); // the first page shows at once
root.querySelector('.to-orders').events.register('press', () => outlet.show(ordersPage()));
root.querySelector('.to-customers').events.register('press', () => outlet.show(customersPage()));

// A page loads its data as it would anyway: a jl-load-state and load().
function ordersPage() {
  const page = document.createElement('section');
  const state = document.createElement('jl-load-state');
  page.append(state);
  state.load({ fetch: () => api.orders(), draw: (orders) => drawRows(state, orders) });
  return page;
}
```
